# Code Royale

> A free, open source multiplayer coding game. Friends join a room, get the
> same challenge and the same clock, and the most hidden tests passed wins.

Code Royale is played at https://coderoyale.app, in the browser, with no
account. It was made by Eduardo Kairalla to play with friends in spare time.

## How a match works

- One player creates a room and shares its code or link.
- The host picks the difficulties (easy, medium, hard or any mix) and starts
  the round.
- Everyone gets the same challenge and the same time limit.
- Players write a solution in Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, Java, C,
  C++ or Rust, with autocomplete, and can run it against the public examples
  as often as they like.
- Each player submits once, against hidden tests. When time runs out, what is
  in the editor is submitted automatically.
- The most tests passed wins; the fastest submission breaks ties. After the
  round, everyone can read everyone's code.

## Project

- [Source code](https://github.com/eduardokairalla1/code-royale): MIT
  licensed; frontend in React and TypeScript, backend in Node with Fastify
  and Socket.IO, a Go service for language servers, Redis for state, and
  Piston to run player code.
- [README](https://github.com/eduardokairalla1/code-royale/blob/main/README.md):
  how it works and how to run it with Docker Compose.
- [Contributing](https://github.com/eduardokairalla1/code-royale/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md):
  how to add a challenge or send a fix.
- [Security](https://github.com/eduardokairalla1/code-royale/blob/main/SECURITY.md):
  how to report a vulnerability.

## Notes

- Rooms live at /game/<code>. They are private, temporary, and not meant to
  be indexed.
- There are no accounts, ads or payments.
